chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Dickie Wells, who almost talked on the trombone
summary: Wells came through Springfield with Cecil Scott, later played with Teddy Hill and Basie, and kidded Vic Dickinson.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: And J. J. -- well, of course, we're going way back.
Dickie Wells. I want to talk about Dickie Wells for a while.

Dickie Wells came through my home with Cecil Scott. I thought he was the most phenomenal trombone player I had ever heard. He was making a lot of glisses and he was -- he could almost do a conversation with the horn. Then later on when I heard him, he had left Cecil and he went with Teddy Hill. Then later he went with Basie and stayed with Basie a long time. He did a lot of good recordings with Basie, a lot of good recordings.
And, of course, Vic got a chance to play with Basie, too.

Dickie liked to kid a lot, you know, and he used to kid Vic a lot. One time they were sitting on the stage and Vic was sitting there -- he had stayed up all night and he was asleep, you know -- and Dickie shook him and said, 'Hey, it's your time to play.' And it wasn't his solo but he grabbed his horn up and started playing.
